source: WHO Model List of Essential Medicines (23rd List Reference + Sri Lanka National Formulary Cross-Reference)
licence_note: WHO Essential Medicines List (Non-commercial / clinical reference use). Check NMRA Sri Lanka for local registered brand packs.

ibuprofen.recommended_indications: Acute/chronic pain, fever, inflammatory conditions, migraine
ibuprofen.who_notes: Not recommended in children under 3 months. Avoid in active peptic ulceration, severe heart/renal/hepatic failure, and third trimester of pregnancy.
ibuprofen.typical_adult_dose: 200 mg to 400 mg orally every 4-6 hours as needed (max 1200 mg/day OTC; up to 2400 mg/day under medical supervision).

acetaminophen.who_notes: First-line analgesic/antipyretic. Hepatotoxicity risk in overdose (>4000 mg/day in adults) or hepatic impairment.
acetaminophen.typical_adult_dose: 500 mg to 1000 mg every 4-6 hours as needed (Maximum 4000 mg/24 hours; 2000 mg/24 hours in chronic liver disease).

aspirin.recommended_indications: Acute coronary syndrome, secondary cardiovascular prevention, acute migraine/pain
aspirin.who_notes: Contraindicated in children <16 years due to Reye syndrome risk, active GI bleeding, hemophilia. Increased bleeding risk with anticoagulants (warfarin, DOACs) and other NSAIDs.
aspirin.typical_adult_dose: Antiplatelet: 75 mg to 100 mg once daily (150-300 mg loading dose in ACS). Analgesic: 300-600 mg every 4-6 hours (max 4000 mg/day).

diclofenac.eml_status: Not on WHO EML (Replaced by ibuprofen/naproxen due to CV risk; widely used in Sri Lanka NMRA formulary)
diclofenac.recommended_indications: Acute musculoskeletal pain, osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis
diclofenac.who_notes: Higher cardiovascular thrombotic risk and GI ulceration risk compared to ibuprofen/naproxen. Contraindicated in established ischemic heart disease, cerebrovascular disease, and active GI bleed.

warfarin.recommended_indications: Venous thromboembolism (DVT/PE), atrial fibrillation, mechanical heart valves
warfarin.who_notes: Narrow therapeutic index; requires regular INR monitoring. Major bleeding risk when combined with NSAIDs (ibuprofen, diclofenac, naproxen, aspirin), antiplatelets, metronidazole, fluconazole, macrolides, or amiodarone. Teratogenic in pregnancy.
warfarin.typical_adult_dose: Typically 2 mg to 10 mg orally once daily, strictly individualized according to INR target (usually 2.0-3.0).

clopidogrel.recommended_indications: Acute coronary syndrome, coronary stenting, secondary stroke/MI prevention
clopidogrel.who_notes: CYP2C19 prodrug: avoid concomitant omeprazole or esomeprazole which inhibit CYP2C19 and reduce antiplatelet efficacy (use pantoprazole or famotidine instead). High bleeding risk with anticoagulants and NSAIDs.
clopidogrel.typical_adult_dose: 75 mg orally once daily (300-600 mg loading dose in ACS).

amoxicillin.recommended_indications: Community-acquired pneumonia, otitis media, sinusitis, strep pharyngitis, H. pylori eradication
amoxicillin.who_notes: First-choice Access antibiotic. Contraindicated in patients with history of penicillin hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis.
amoxicillin.typical_adult_dose: 250 mg to 500 mg every 8 hours, or 500 mg to 1000 mg every 12 hours.

azithromycin.recommended_indications: Atypical pneumonia, chlamydia, cholera, enteric fever (typhoid)
azithromycin.who_notes: Watch group antibiotic—reserve for specific indications due to resistance risk. Prolongs QT interval; caution with other QT-prolonging drugs (amiodarone, ondansetron, fluoroquinolones).
azithromycin.typical_adult_dose: 500 mg once daily for 3 days, or 500 mg on day 1 followed by 250 mg on days 2-5.

ciprofloxacin.recommended_indications: Complicated UTI, pyelonephritis, invasive gastrointestinal infections, Pseudomonas infections
ciprofloxacin.who_notes: Risk of tendinitis/tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy, CNS effects, and QT prolongation. Chelated by antacids, calcium, iron, zinc (separate doses by 2 hours). Inhibits CYP1A2 and increases warfarin bleeding risk.
ciprofloxacin.typical_adult_dose: 250 mg to 750 mg orally every 12 hours depending on infection severity.

metronidazole.recommended_indications: Anaerobic bacterial infections, C. difficile, amoebiasis, giardiasis, trichomoniasis
metronidazole.who_notes: Strict alcohol avoidance (disulfiram-like reaction during and 48h after therapy). Potentiates warfarin anticoagulant effect (increases INR/bleeding).
metronidazole.typical_adult_dose: 400 mg to 500 mg orally every 8 hours (or 7.5 mg/kg every 8 hours; max 4000 mg/day).

metformin.recommended_indications: First-line management of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
metformin.who_notes: Contraindicated in severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m2), acute metabolic acidosis, or decompensated heart/liver failure due to lactic acidosis risk. Hold prior to iodinated contrast procedures if eGFR < 60.
metformin.typical_adult_dose: Start 500 mg once or twice daily with meals; titrate up to maximum 2000-2550 mg/day in divided doses.

amlodipine.recommended_indications: Hypertension, chronic stable or vasospastic angina
amlodipine.who_notes: Calcium channel blocker. Limits simvastatin co-administration dose to max 20 mg/day due to myopathy/rhabdomyolysis risk.
amlodipine.typical_adult_dose: 5 mg once daily; may increase to maximum 10 mg once daily.

losartan.who_notes: Contraindicated in pregnancy (fetotoxic). Avoid combining with ACE inhibitors (enalapril/lisinopril). Monitor potassium and renal function, especially if combined with spironolactone or NSAIDs ('triple whammy' acute kidney injury risk).
losartan.typical_adult_dose: 50 mg once daily (25 mg in volume depletion); max 100 mg/day.

enalapril.recommended_indications: Hypertension, heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, proteinuric CKD
enalapril.who_notes: Contraindicated in pregnancy, history of angioedema, bilateral renal artery stenosis. High hyperkalemia risk with spironolactone/potassium supplements; acute kidney injury risk with NSAIDs + diuretics.
enalapril.typical_adult_dose: 2.5 mg to 5 mg once or twice daily, titrated up to 10-20 mg twice daily (max 40 mg/day).

furosemide.recommended_indications: Edema due to heart failure, hepatic cirrhosis, renal disease; acute pulmonary edema
furosemide.who_notes: Monitor electrolytes (hypokalemia, hyponatremia), fluid status, and renal function. Ototoxicity risk at high IV doses or with aminoglycosides.
furosemide.typical_adult_dose: 20 mg to 80 mg orally once or twice daily, titrated to clinical response (max 600 mg/day in severe edematous states).

spironolactone.recommended_indications: Heart failure (HFrEF), ascites in cirrhosis, primary hyperaldosteronism, resistant hypertension
spironolactone.who_notes: Risk of severe hyperkalemia, especially in renal impairment or when combined with ACE inhibitors (enalapril/lisinopril) or ARBs (losartan/valsartan).
spironolactone.typical_adult_dose: Heart failure: 25 mg to 50 mg once daily. Cirrhosis/ascites: 100 mg to 400 mg/day.

atorvastatin.recommended_indications: Hypercholesterolemia, primary and secondary prevention of cardiovascular events
atorvastatin.who_notes: Contraindicated in active liver disease and pregnancy. Risk of myopathy/rhabdomyolysis increased by CYP3A4 inhibitors (clarithromycin, itraconazole, cyclosporine, gemfibrozil).
atorvastatin.typical_adult_dose: 10 mg to 80 mg orally once daily.

simvastatin.who_notes: Strong CYP3A4 substrate: contraindicated with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (clarithromycin, itraconazole). Do not exceed 20 mg daily when co-administered with amlodipine or amiodarone.
simvastatin.typical_adult_dose: 10 mg to 40 mg orally once daily in the evening (80 mg restricted due to myopathy risk).

omeprazole.recommended_indications: Peptic ulcer disease, GERD, Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, NSAID ulcer prophylaxis, H. pylori eradication
omeprazole.who_notes: Inhibits CYP2C19: avoid co-administration with clopidogrel (reduces active clopidogrel metabolite and antiplatelet protection).
omeprazole.typical_adult_dose: 20 mg to 40 mg orally once daily before a meal.

prednisolone.recommended_indications: Acute asthma/COPD exacerbation, autoimmune/inflammatory disorders, allergic conditions
prednisolone.who_notes: Increases GI ulceration/bleeding risk when combined with NSAIDs or aspirin. Causes hyperglycemia (monitor diabetic patients). Taper gradually if used >2-3 weeks.
prednisolone.typical_adult_dose: 5 mg to 60 mg orally daily depending on indication (e.g., 40 mg daily for 5 days in acute asthma).
